issuer.name: Immersve (card issuing partner for Europe and LATAM; regulated issuing entity not named)

funding.supported_assets_note: Europe/LATAM (Immersve) cards are 'funded via USDC on the Base network'; the card page also lists USDT, ETH and SOL as top-up assets. Top-ups are converted to a USD card balance (0-fees article: 'USDC/USDT top-ups converted to USD'). Spending in EUR/GBP therefore involves a currency conversion.

eligibility.usage_note: Card page (2026): 'Europe: EEA and UK'. The 2025-06-18 launch article names the 31 countries listed here (UK + all 30 EEA members) as eligible regions. The 2026-10-13 academy guide says 'the supported country list is determined dynamically within the Bitget Wallet app'. Other regions (LATAM, APAC, South Africa, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Mainland China) use different issuing partners and are not modelled in this variant.

kyc.stages_note: KYC inside the Bitget Wallet app before the card is issued: 18+; passport, driver's licence or national ID plus face verification; country, address, contact details and estimated monthly spend declared. 'No credit checks or staking required.' Approval 'as little as one minute' / 'within 3 minutes'. Proof of address not mentioned for Europe.

access.note: '0 annual fee', 'no monthly card fee'. Single tier; the 3% 'Booster' assetback is a conditional upgrade, not a paid tier.

fees.conditions: No issuance fee stated for the European virtual card on any page read (the Mainland China fee article states none; the APAC physical card costs $49, $25 until 2026-12-31 — other regions, not applied).
'0 annual fee. No interest markup, no monthly card fee, no hidden charges' (card page); 'No annual fee' (academy guide); 'No annual fees' (EU launch article).

Standard FX rate for Europe not published on any page read: the Europe 'Fees' help-centre article could not be reached (see research list). The '0 Fees' programme refunds 'any FX fee charged' on spend within a monthly cap of 400 USD (600 USD for MOEW campaign members); 'standard fee rates apply' above it. Settlement 'closely matches Google's live rates'. Mainland China article: FX 'usually around 1%' — other region, not applied.

Virtual-only card in Europe; a 'Refunds and cash withdrawals' help article exists for the Europe/Africa/LATAM section but could not be reached. APAC physical card: 1% or 5 USD minimum — other region, not applied.

EU launch article (2025-06-18): 'no top-up fees'. '0 Fees' article (2025-11-17): top-up/conversion fees on USDC/USDT 'refunded when you spend' within the 400 USD monthly cap, standard rates above it — implying a standard top-up fee exists whose rate is not published for Europe (Mainland China: 1%). Treated as unknown; contradiction between 'no top-up fees' and 'refunded within a cap' recorded.

editorial.summary: Virtual Mastercard for EEA and UK residents, issued through Bitget Wallet's partner Immersve and prefunded with USDC on Base into a USD balance. 2% 'assetback' on all spend (3% for new users or above a monthly spend threshold) paid in a chosen asset (BTC, gold, tokenized US stocks or USDC), no annual or monthly fee. The European fee schedule (FX, top-up, cash withdrawal) is not published on any page the run could read: FX and top-up fees are refunded only within a 400 USD monthly spend cap, and standard rates apply above it.
good_for: EEA/UK residents who already hold USDC on Base and want a free virtual Mastercard with Apple Pay / Google Pay
Small monthly spend (under the 400 USD fee-refund cap) where FX and top-up fees are refunded
Users who want rewards in BTC, gold or tokenized stocks rather than a provider token
not_for: Anyone who needs a physical card in Europe (virtual only; physical cards exist only in 8 APAC countries)
Spending above 400 USD a month without knowing the standard FX and top-up rates (not published for Europe)
Users who need a named regulated issuer: only the partner Immersve is named
watch_outs: The card balance is in USD; EUR/GBP purchases are currency conversions whose standard rate is not published for Europe (Mainland China article: ~1%; APAC: 1.7% + 0.05%).
'No top-up fees' (2025 launch article) conflicts with the 2025-11 '0 Fees' programme that refunds top-up fees only within a monthly cap — both pages are official; the fee is modelled as unknown.
The Booster 3% rate depends on a monthly spend threshold stated only as '$200–$400' in a FAQ; the current rule is 'displayed on the card page' in the app.
Reward limits ('reward limits', 'applicable limits') are mentioned but never quantified.
Issuer status is a hypothesis: Immersve is named as issuing partner, the licensed Mastercard issuer is not.
The welcome bonus 'up to $20' is recorded at its maximum with status hypothesis; rules not read.
Help-centre articles are only readable under a locale path (e.g. /es-AR/helpCenter/<id>); the Europe Fees article needs a browser read.
